title: Ways to invest
log: 2026-11-04T09:36:48Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new
2026-11-04T18:10:11Z recheck: the fresh check agreed with the fix, cleared with the fix

match.reason: The bank point teaches that a business must beat the return on alternatives such as a bank account, shares or property, but it does not cover the new point's list of ways to invest (term deposits, managed funds, superannuation) or its focus on investing for future income.

draft.title: Ways to invest
card: To invest is to put money into something now, hoping it will give you more money or value in the future. Income can come as payments, or as a rise in the value of what you own.
a share is a small part of ownership in a company. Owners may get a payment from the company's profit, and the share price can rise or fall.
money lent to a bank for a set time at an agreed rate of interest. The bank pays the interest and returns the money at the end.
a pool of money from many people, which professionals invest in a mix of things such as shares and property.
draft.remember: Investing means using money now to build future income. Shares, term deposits and managed funds are different ways to do it.

a.q: Which of these is an example of investing?
opts: Lending money to a bank for a set time to earn interest
Spending savings on a holiday with friends
Paying a phone bill at the end of the month
Keeping cash in a drawer for a few years
a.why: A term deposit puts money into something now to earn interest later. A holiday and a phone bill are spending, and cash in a drawer earns nothing.
a.clue: Which choice is meant to earn more money later?

b.q: Tom has a little money. He wants a professional to spread it across many shares and other assets with the money of many other people. What should he choose?
opts: A managed fund
A term deposit
A single share
A phone plan
b.why: A managed fund pools money from many people and professionals invest it in a mix of things. A term deposit is a loan to a bank for a set time. A single share is ownership of only one company.
b.clue: Think about pooled money run by professionals.

a.best: Lending money to a bank for a set time to earn interest

problems.detail: The point lists five ways to invest: shares, term deposits, managed funds, property and superannuation. The card covers only the first three and leaves out property and superannuation.

The remember line names only shares, term deposits and managed funds as ways to invest. It leaves out property and superannuation, which the point includes, so students may think there are only three ways.

check.summary: Both questions are sound and each has one clear right answer. The card and remember line leave out property and superannuation, two of the five ways to invest that this point is meant to teach.

proposal.title: Ways to invest
card: To invest is to put money into something now, hoping it will give you more money or value in the future. Income can come as payments, or as a rise in the value of what you own.

A share is a small part of ownership in a company. Owners may get a payment from its profit, and the share price can rise or fall. A term deposit is money lent to a bank for a set time at an agreed interest rate.
A managed fund pools money from many people, and professionals invest it in a mix such as shares and property. Property, such as a house or flat, can earn rent and may rise in value.
Superannuation, or super, is money saved for retirement. Employers pay part of a worker's wages into a super fund, which invests it until the worker retires.
proposal.remember: Shares, term deposits, managed funds, property and super are five ways to use money now to build future income.

a.q: Which of these is an example of investing?
opts: Lending money to a bank for a set time to earn interest
Spending savings on a holiday with friends
Paying a phone bill at the end of the month
Keeping cash in a drawer for a few years
a.why: A term deposit puts money into something now to earn interest later. A holiday and a phone bill are spending. Cash in a drawer is saved, but it earns no payments and does not grow in value.
a.clue: Which choice is meant to earn more money later?

b.q: Ali buys a flat in Hobart and rents it to a tenant. How might this investment give him income?
opts: Rent payments and a rise in the flat's value
Interest from a bank and a rise in the flat's value
A share of company profit and rent payments
Wages from his employer and bank interest
b.why: Property can earn rent and may rise in value, so Ali can gain both ways. Interest from a bank comes from a term deposit, and a share of company profit comes from owning shares, not from owning a flat.
b.clue: What does a tenant pay, and what can happen to a flat's price?

a.best: Lending money to a bank for a set time to earn interest

b.best: Rent payments and a rise in the flat's value
